quote: try { localStorage.setItem(BACKUP_KEY, raw); } catch (e) { /* storage is already failing; the load message says so */ }
title: A failed backup of unreadable data is swallowed, and the load message still says the data was kept
evidence: store.js:30 ignores the result of the backup write. The three callers (store.js:47, :52, :66) then return messages that state the data 'was kept under notes-backup'. The comment says the load message covers a failing store, but none of those messages does: only the getItem-blocked branch at store.js:39 mentions storage. saveNotes (store.js:73) overwrites STORAGE_KEY on the next edit.
failing_case: STORAGE_KEY holds a 3 MB truncated JSON string (a half-finished write). Copying it to 'notes-backup' needs about 3 MB more, so the origin quota is exceeded and setItem throws QuotaExceededError. The catch drops the error. loadNotes returns 'Saved notes could not be read. The unreadable data was kept under "notes-backup".' The user clicks New note. saveNotes replaces STORAGE_KEY with a small valid object. The only copy of the old notes is gone, and the app told the user it was kept.
remediation: Have backupRaw return whether the write succeeded and put that into the message ('could not be copied, the original is untouched'). Do not let saveNotes overwrite STORAGE_KEY until a backup exists or the user agrees to discard it.

title: Every save writes the whole in-memory list over storage; a second tab silently erases the first tab's notes
evidence: app.js:18 loads `notes` once. Every commit (app.js:33) serialises that array and replaces the stored value. app.js has no `storage` event listener and does no re-read or merge before writing (grep: no 'storage' listener in app.js).
failing_case: Open the app in tab 1 and tab 2 (both show note A). In tab 1 click New note and type 'Plan'. It saves. In tab 2, edit note A's body and wait 500 ms. Tab 2's flushSave calls saveNotes with its own list [A], which does not contain 'Plan'. The stored data now has only A. Tab 2 shows 'Saved'. 'Plan' is gone after the next reload. Deletes behave the same in the other direction (a deleted note comes back).
remediation: Re-read storage and merge by id (newest `updated` wins) inside commit, and listen for the `storage` event to refresh the list. Alternatively write one key per note so each tab writes only the record it changed.

title: 'Search notes' only searches titles, never note bodies
evidence: The control is labelled 'Search notes' (index.html:14). renderList filters on n.title only. The empty state reads 'No notes match ...' (app.js:87) without saying titles only.
failing_case: A note titled 'Untitled' holds the body 'dentist 3pm Tuesday'. Type 'dentist' in Search notes. The list shows 'No notes match "dentist".' although the text exists in a saved note.
remediation: Match against title and body, or relabel the field 'Search titles' and make the empty state say so.

requirement.why: The label says 'Search notes' and the app stores a body for each note; no spec was supplied.

title: Opening or deleting a note rebuilds the whole list, so keyboard focus falls back to the page start
evidence: The click handler (app.js:161) calls selectNote or deleteNote, which call renderList (app.js:100, :121). renderList replaces every button, including the one that has focus. Nothing restores focus, and selectNote does not move focus to the editor. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order.
failing_case: Keyboard only: Tab to the second note's button and press Enter. The note loads, but the focused button is removed from the DOM and focus resets to the document start. To type in the note the user must Tab through search and New note, and then through every Delete and note button, to reach the title. After Delete and confirm, focus is lost the same way.
remediation: After renderList, refocus the button with the same data-id (or the next one after a delete). Better: update the existing list items and only change the aria-current attribute. Move focus to #title on selection by keyboard.

title: Search results and empty-state text are not announced; the shared-notes live region is revealed and filled in one step
evidence: #empty has no role=status or aria-live, yet app.js:86-89 writes 'No notes match ...' into it on every keystroke. #shared-status (index.html:22) sits inside a section that is `hidden` until app.js:139 unhides it, and the text is set at app.js:140 in the same task. WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA). The 'Saving…' message (app.js:56) is re-set on every keystroke.
failing_case: A screen-reader user types 'zzz' in Search notes. The list empties and 'No notes match "zzz".' appears, but nothing is spoken. The first shared-notes search reveals the box and fills its status in the same task, so the 'Searching shared notes…' and result text are often not announced. While typing in the editor, 'Saving…' is replaced with identical text on each keystroke and may be re-read.
remediation: Make #empty a role=status region that is always in the DOM (empty, not `hidden`), and keep #shared-status in a live region outside the hidden container. Set 'Saving…' only when the text changes.

title: At phone width the editor sits below an unbounded note list, and choosing a note shows nothing
evidence: Below 720 px (styles.css:20) the layout is a single column: toolbar, then #list (no max-height or scroll), then the editor. app.js selectNote (app.js:92-101) fills the editor but does not scroll or focus it.
failing_case: At 390 px with 40 notes (about 36 px each plus gaps, over 1,400 px of list), tap a note near the top. The row gets a highlight, and the title and body fill in far below the fold. The user sees no result and may tap again. The same happens after New note, where focus() does scroll, but not when opening an existing note.
remediation: On narrow screens cap the list (max-height with overflow:auto) or show list and editor as separate views. Call els.title.focus({preventScroll:false}) or scrollIntoView on the editor when a note is opened.

title: A new or edited note disappears from the list while the search filter hides it, and the list says 'No notes match' while the user is editing one
evidence: createNote() (app.js:103-111) does not clear els.search, and renderList() (app.js:59-90) filters by the current search text. The new note is selected and focused but filtered out. The same happens when a title edit stops matching the query.
failing_case: Type 'abc' in Search notes (2 matches), then press New note. The editor opens an 'Untitled' note, but the list still shows only the 'abc' matches. The current note is not listed, so no aria-current row is shown. If nothing matches 'abc', the list is empty and reads 'No notes match "abc".' beside an open, edited note.
remediation: In createNote(), set els.search.value = '' (and clear the shared results) before selecting. Optionally always include the current note in the filtered list.
